language.script_notes: English signage with Hausa spoken by the majority, and Arabic script appearing on mosques, Quranic schools and some shopfronts.

road_furniture.line_paint: Long, straight roads across dry plains with few markings.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Segmented utility poles; state names such as Kano, Yobe and Sokoto appear on shop signs.

architecture.roof_style: Flat mud roofs and corrugated metal on modern buildings; domed and tower forms on mosques.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal on newer buildings; traditional thatch and mud on older ones.
architecture.wall_construction: Sun-dried mud brick (tubali) walls plastered with mud and straw are the classic Hausa building material, with rectilinear courses laid in thick mud mortar; walled family compounds; mosques with mud towers and projecting timber or palm sticks; newer concrete construction in cities.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Earthy tan and ochre mud walls, with white-painted mosque minarets and concrete.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Mosques with minarets in every town; ancient mud-walled cities and compounds (Kano's old city); Emir's palaces; walled family compounds and compound gates with decorative facades.

nature.vegetation: Grassland savanna in the middle belt fading into sparse Sahel scrub in the north; millet fields around Kaduna; few trees and almost no grass in the far-north Sudan zone, with minimal vegetation outside towns.
nature.terrain: Flat, dry plains and rocky outcrops, with the higher granite hills and rocky plateau around Jos; harmattan dust haze during the dry season.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, dry and dusty with a long dry season — a pale, sandy, sparsely vegetated look far from the lush south.

vehicles.plate_format: A northern state name such as Kano or Kaduna along the top.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motorcycles and keke-napep tricycles are ubiquitous; heavy trucks on long-haul routes; donkey and camel carts in some areas.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage exists along main highways and around major cities such as Kano, Kaduna and Abuja's surroundings; the far north is sparser.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Sahel landscape, mud-brick architecture and mosques
confusion_set.tiebreaker: English signage, keke-napep tricycles and segmented utility poles are found here; those neighbours use French signage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture and plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The north has mud-brick compounds, mosques and dry savanna; the south has rainforest, oil palms and dense churches and corrugated-roof towns.
